newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR WEAKER AS PRESSURE CONTINUES.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR WEAKER AS PRESSURE CONTINUES.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar took a further knock against the U.S. currency on Wednesday as import pressure continued pounding the market with little support from the central Reserve Bank, dealers said.
"Basically the dollar is still sliding and dealers are protecting their positions by quoting wide spreads," one dealer said.
"If the central bank is doing anything then it's very little...they are saying the market should correct itself," he added.

Dealers say it is now up to the central bank to bring back stability to the local currency whose free-fall, triggered off last Wednesday by a large import payment, was worsened by central bank governor Leonard Tsumba's statement on Friday that the unit was overvalued.

At around 0820 GMT on Wednesday, the Zimbabwe dollar was trading at 11.6000/7000 on the U.S. dollar from late Tuesday's 11.5500/7500 and was at 18.8510/19.0420 from 18.7600/19.1100 versus pound sterling.
It was however quoted firmer on the mark at 6.2820/3430 compared to 6.3100/4200 and at 2.5160/5410 from 2.5200/5600 against South Africa's rand.
